svg.title: How to get online in Thailand: three questions
svg.desc: Three questions. Question 1: Does your unlocked phone support eSIM, and do you want to call Grab as soon as you land? If yes, buy a tourist eSIM: AIS eSIM starts at THB 399; check official sites for True and third-party prices. Scan the QR code and install it before departure, then enable data roaming after landing. If no, question 2: Are you staying no more than 5 days, using little data, and need verification texts on a Taiwan phone number? If yes, use roaming from a Taiwan carrier: Taiwan Mobile's Southeast Asia plan starts at TWD 129 per day, and Chunghwa Telecom's Southeast Asia volume plan starts at TWD 149 for 1 GB over 15 days. Keep your Taiwan number and do not change the SIM. If no, question 3: Are 3 or more people traveling together, or do you need to tether a laptop? If yes, rent a pocket WiFi for collection and return at Taoyuan Airport and pay by the day, or share one unlimited SIM as a hotspot. If no, buy a physical tourist SIM at an airport counter: True costs THB 449 for 8 days; AIS offers 5, 8, 15, 30, and 60 days. Counters are open 24 hours, and the passport holder must register in person. NBTC notes: the passport holder must appear in person, each carrier allows up to 3 SIMs, a tourist SIM is valid for at most 60 days and cannot be extended by topping up, and online eSIM purchases also require a passport upload. Data estimates: maps and messaging use a few hundred MB per day, social media and photo uploads about 1 GB per day, and video or hotspot use 3 GB or more per day, so choose unlimited data. Prices were checked on official websites on September 13, 2026.
